WMT.rationale: Walmart is a fundamentally sound, high-quality business with durable competitive advantages (scale, grocery dominance, growing high-margin advertising/membership streams, 53-year dividend streak). However, the valuation has become extremely stretched relative to the company's actual earnings power. At a P/E of ~54x (near the top of its 32.6–55.3 range over the past year), P/B of 11.6x, and earnings yield of just 1.9%, the stock is priced for perfection — more like a high-growth technology company than a mature retailer generating ~3–5% revenue growth. The P/E has expanded from ~33x a year ago to ~54x today, a 60%+ multiple expansion that far outpaces the ~35% YoY EPS growth. Multiple independent valuation frameworks (DCF, economic profit) suggest intrinsic values in the $83 range, and even bull-case analysts acknowledge the stock is 'narrative-driven rather than fundamentals-driven' at current levels. Key risks are heavily tilted to the downside: tariff exposure on Asian-sourced general merchandise, rising oil prices ($98/bbl WTI) pressuring Walmart's massive trucking/fuel costs (>$100M headwind already cited), Maximum Fair Pricing legislation creating a ~100bp revenue headwind, and grocery market share erosion (from 20.4% in 2024 to 19.9% in 2026 per Numerator). The Q1 FY2027 earnings report (expected ~May 14) is a near-term downside catalyst — management pre-guided for lower Q1 operating income growth due to tariff timing, and any margin miss at this multiple will be severely punished. The combination of extreme valuation, deteriorating near-term fundamentals (tariffs, fuel costs, share loss), and a likely de-rating catalyst makes this one of the most asymmetrically negative risk/reward setups in large-cap retail.

Our DCF and Economic Profit models produce a consistent intrinsic value of $83.24 as of today. The relative model is the only methodology that produces any scenario approaching the current price, and only when using the PEG method with aggressive growth assumptions, further reinforcing our view that the current valuation is narrative-driven rather than fundamentals-driven.

At 43x forward earnings, Walmart isn't being valued on what it earns today. It's being valued on a future where advertising and membership keep expanding their share of profits. Any slowdown in that shift, or gross margin pressure from tariffs on general merchandise, gets penalized hard at this multiple. Management has already pre-guided for lower Q1 operating income growth due to tariff timing, and Maximum Fair Pricing legislation on pharmacy is expected to create a 100 basis point revenue headwind for the full fiscal year.
Walmart's leading share of the grocery market continues to decline, according to the latest data from Numerator. Walmart currently holds a 19.9% share, down from 20% in 2025 and 20.4% in 2024.
Walmart maintains one of the largest trucking operations globally, and the company has suffered a fuel headwind in excess of $100 million over the last quarter
Walmart is expected to post earnings of $0.65 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +6.6%
